findings.title: Light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 70% for embedded post author links
findings.body: The diff replaces `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The light-theme branch should stay at 30%, with the dark branch being `$secondary` at 70%. This PR is meant to leave light themes unchanged, but these links become much lighter and less readable there. The dark branch is also inverted: 30% on $secondary is far too dark for a dark theme.

findings.title: group-member-info .name light lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: The original light-theme color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new code uses 50%/50% for both light and dark. The light theme therefore changes unintentionally and `.name` is no longer visually distinct from `.title`. The correct pair is 30% for `$primary` and 70% for `$secondary`.

findings.title: Mobile group-member-info .name light lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: This is the same regression as in desktop/user.scss. The light-theme color shifts from 30% to 50% lightness, so the PR changes the light theme's appearance. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: custom-message-length light value changed from 70% to 30%
findings.body: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new light branch is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, with `$secondary` at 70%. The light-theme color becomes much darker, which is an unintended regression, and the dark pair is mismatched with the desktop version. The correct pair is 70%/30%, matching desktop/modal.scss.

findings.title: topic-map h3 light lightness changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: The original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The new code uses 50%/50%. The light theme's h3 gets lighter and loses contrast with h4. The correct pair is 20%/80%, as used for the desktop topic-map h3.
